docs.title: Adaptive Competitive Programming Pattern Retention System
docs.text:
CP Recall is a browser extension and companion dashboard that helps competitive programmers retain the patterns behind the problems they solve, not just the problems themselves.

The system works alongside platforms like LeetCode, tracking pattern-level mastery and using spaced repetition to resurface a different problem from the same pattern family when a concept is due for review — testing true understanding and transfer, not memorized solutions.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Competitive programmers solve hundreds of problems, but often forget the underlying patterns weeks later.

Existing platforms track problems solved, not whether the pattern behind them has actually been retained.

CP Recall solves this by treating patterns — not individual problems — as the unit of learning and review.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
CP Recall aims to:

  • Track pattern-level mastery of DSA / competitive programming patterns
  • Schedule reviews using FSRS (Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler)
  • Surface a different problem from the same pattern family to test retention and transfer
  • Integrate directly into the existing LeetCode workflow via a browser extension

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. The browser extension detects when a problem is solved on LeetCode and tags it with its underlying pattern.
  2. FSRS calculates when each pattern is next due for review based on performance.
  3. When a pattern is due, CP Recall surfaces a new, unseen problem from the same pattern family.
  4. Review status is shown directly on the Home Dashboard, Pattern Dashboard, Problem Library, and Problem Details — no separate revision screen needed.

Team Nexus 3 — Subham Kumar, Tanush Grover, Shubhi Singh

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
# Features

## Browser Extension

A lightweight extension that runs alongside LeetCode — not a permanently visible sidebar — and detects when a problem has been solved.

---

## Pattern Tagging

Solved problems are automatically tagged with their underlying DSA / competitive programming pattern (e.g. sliding window, two pointers, DP on trees).

---

## FSRS-Based Review Scheduling

Uses the Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler (FSRS), not the older SM-2 algorithm, to calculate when each pattern is due for review based on past performance.

---

## Adaptive Retrieval Practice

Example:

"Pattern: Sliding Window is due for review"

Instead of repeating the same problem, CP Recall surfaces a **different, unseen problem** from the same pattern family — testing transfer, not memorization.

---

## Integrated Dashboards

Review information is woven directly into the existing views rather than a separate revision screen:

- Home Dashboard

- Pattern Dashboard

- Problem Library

- Problem Details

---

## Progress Tracking

Users can see pattern-level mastery over time, not just a raw count of problems solved.

docs.title: Problem statement
docs.text:
# Problem Statement

## The Problem

Competitive programmers solve large numbers of problems but often struggle to retain the underlying patterns.

Students and job-seekers preparing for technical interviews frequently forget:

- Which pattern a problem belonged to

- How to recognize that pattern in a new, unseen problem

- Why a particular approach worked, weeks after solving it

---

## Limitations of Existing Solutions

### LeetCode Progress Tracking

These platforms track the number of problems solved, not whether the underlying pattern has actually been retained.

### Generic Spaced Repetition Apps (e.g. Anki)

General-purpose spaced repetition tools are not tailored to competitive programming and require manual card creation for every pattern.

### Manual Notes

Manually maintained notes or spreadsheets require significant discipline and do not adapt scheduling to individual performance.

---

## Proposed Solution

CP Recall creates a pattern-level memory layer over a user's competitive programming activity.

Instead of tracking raw problem counts, CP Recall tracks mastery of the *patterns* behind those problems and schedules reviews using FSRS.

Example:

"You solved a sliding window problem three weeks ago — here's a new one to test whether you still recognize the pattern."

CP Recall surfaces the right problem at the right time to reinforce long-term retention.
